title: America's Army Reserve Soldiers provide relief support after Hurricane Irma
description: ORLANDO, Florida – U.S. Army Reserve Soldiers distribute cases of bottled water to residents of Merritt Island, Florida, Sep. 14, 2017, in the aftermath of of Hurricane Irma, Sep. 13, 2017. The Army Reserve Soldiers from the 143rd Sustainment Command (Expeditionary) and the 329th Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear Company received a mission assignment to provide support to Merritt Island, which is still without a clean, safe water supply. U.S. Army Reserve Soldiers are agile and mission-capable, regularly training to safely operate the LMTVs on rigorous terrain and under hazardous conditions to provide support to state and local authorities.

transcript.text: - [Sgt. Gonzales] U.S. Army Reserve soldiers from the 329th
Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Company
receive orders to assist Florida residents
affected by Hurricane Irma.
(engine starting)
- Our main mission here in the 329th
once we got boots on ground
was to get the vehicles up and running.
We devised a plan to get the vehicles refueled,
PNCS, ready to go and ensure that safety is number one,
'cause if we can't make it out there, we can't do our job.
Ensuring that the soldiers were adequately trained
and licensed on these vehicles,
and ensuring that they had their full load out
and packing so that they can take care of themselves
while performing these missions,
so that we can all come home safe.
- Currently, we are distributing water to the city.
We have the sheriffs helping out out
with routing all the vehicles.
We get one or two cases per vehicle,
'cause the families here still are under boil water notice.
The help that the Army Reserve is providing,
the community is taking it very well.
They're very appreciative of all
the work we're doing here on ground
for them, and they, you know,
they've come by, thanked us
and some of them have even brought gifts.
- [Sgt. Gonzales] Reporting from Orlando, Florida
for the U.S. Army Reserve Command Public Affairs Office,
I'm U.S. Army Reserve Staff Sergeant Erick Gonzales.
